featured_videos.title: Three Years On Carnivore Changed My Life... Now I'm Testing Something New
featured_videos.creator: StevenSteph
featured_videos.editorial_title: Three Years On Carnivore Changed My Life... Now I'm Testing Something New
featured_videos.commentary: Three years in and Steph's still experimenting instead of coasting, which is honestly the vibe we need more of. The comment section is full of people hitting their own carniversaries (shout out to Rita and her partner at 76 and 81. that's what "staying capable" actually looks like), and it's a good reminder that this isn't about perfection or chasing some ideal physique. It's about showing up better for the people you care about. Love that he's testing new things, because the whole point is finding what keeps *you* strong and clear, not following someone else's script. That's real.

featured_videos.title: How To Fuel Your Body Efficiently / Chicken Sausage Patty Recipe / Nachos!
featured_videos.creator: Low Carb Revelation
featured_videos.editorial_title: How To Fuel Your Body Efficiently / Chicken Sausage Patty Recipe / Nachos!
featured_videos.commentary: Paula nailed something that doesn't get enough airtime: how your body actually *uses* the food you eat, and why that order matters way more than the "calories in, calories out" crowd wants to admit. The chicken sausage recipe and nachos aren't just tasty, they're teaching moments about protein use and real satiety. What struck me most was the community's reaction, though. People aren't just loving the food they're seeing how *easy* this becomes when you stop fighting your body's signals. That's the quiet win nobody talks about, and it's why the "one-size-fits-all" comment hit so hard. When people see someone like Paula moving freely, cooking confidently, and genuinely enjoying family time without the diet stress, that's contagious.

featured_videos.title: Teaching Carnivore to an Entire Amish Community!
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: Teaching Carnivore to an Entire Amish Community!
featured_videos.commentary: What gets me about this is how Kerry framed it: rescuing people from metabolic disease the same way he'd pull someone from a burning car. The comments are picking up on that. and they're right. When you see an entire community suddenly understanding carb addiction ("Battling with Carb Addiction. Please Lord Set me free") and making the connection between their farm animals' behavior and human ketosis, you're watching something shift. The Amish have strong community structures already, which means if this takes root, it spreads differently than it does in fragmented urban America. That's not just reaching individuals, that's potentially changing how a whole culture approaches food and health together.

featured_videos.title: Finally Trying Oat Fiber to Make Keto Tortillas!
featured_videos.creator: Keto Twins
featured_videos.editorial_title: Finally Trying Oat Fiber to Make Keto Tortillas!
featured_videos.commentary: The community came through with the real gold here, and it's worth paying attention to. Someone shared freezing and blitzing the mozzarella before you mix it in, and another commenter nailed the technique of combining eggs with dry ingredients first, then adding to the cheese. These small tweaks matter because they're the difference between wrestling with a greasy mess and actually having something workable. The tortilla press win at the end says it all, too. People aren't just trying recipes, they're thinking about how to make them *practical* for their actual kitchen and their actual life. That's the energy that keeps keto real.

featured_videos.title: The Carnivore Diet Fixes Everything… Doesn’t It?
featured_videos.creator: Doctor Alex
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Carnivore Diet Fixes Everything… Doesn’t It?
featured_videos.commentary: Doctor Alex nails the real debate here, and the comments prove it. You've got people sharing 7-year transformations. migraines gone, 100+ pounds lost, bloodwork that finally makes sense. while others point out that most carnivores didn't jump straight from SAD to all-meat, they transitioned through keto or low-carb first. The honest take? Carnivore works *for some people* in specific contexts, especially those with severe autoimmune issues or metabolic dysfunction, but it's not a universal cure. What matters most is what the boredom comment hints at: sustainability. You can have perfect macros and blood sugar control, but if you hate eating the same three foods, you'll quit. The real win isn't the diet itself. it's finding the eating pattern you'll actually stick to, whether that's carnivore, Mediterranean with some tweaks, or keto with gradual reintroductions. The people getting results aren't chasing the perfect diet; they're chasing consistency.

featured_videos.title: An Update For My 100k+ Subscribers (I've Changed)

featured_videos.editorial_title: An Update For My 100k+ Subscribers (I've Changed)
featured_videos.commentary: What stands out here is how the comments completely flip the script on what creators think their audience wants. Reid's worried about staying "on brand," but his community is basically saying, "We're here for *you*, not the perfectly optimized carnivore content." That's the thing about building real trust. people stick around because they believe in the person, not because you're locked into one lane forever. The recipes will always be there. What matters is that he's honest about what he's actually interested in making next, and his people have already said they're in for the ride.
